days.cardio_note: Members build from a longer Moderate distance into a shorter Hard push — the reduced target at Hard intensity makes the effort feel achievable while still driving cardiovascular output.
Coach members to use the Moderate interval to build into the effort — arriving at Hard already elevated means they can hit it hard and recover fully in the Easy before going again.
Coach members to use the Moderate to climb through Hard and arrive at Max already loaded — the :30 is short enough to give everything they have before resetting in the Easy.
Short Hard bursts followed by longer Moderate recovery bring heart rate down enough that members can sustain quality effort through all four rounds.
Coach members to bank their energy in the Easy interval — the calorie target at Hard is the work, so they should arrive ready to attack it.
Push members to maintain effort through the Moderate so heart rate is already climbing when they hit Max — that's what turns a short burst into a true max effort.
:30 sprints past current threshold will increase aerobic capacity over time.  1:30 total recovery allows consistency in Max efforts.
Moderate is a pace members could hold for many minutes — hard is where it starts to feel unsustainable. Repeating that shift trains the body to recover faster and sustain higher efforts over time.
The moderate-to-hard progression gradually builds fatigue across three rounds. The final max effort under fatigue forces the body to recruit fast-twitch muscle fibers, improving power output.
The longer moderate intervals keep members right at the edge of sustainable effort before the hard pushes past it. Repeating this twice drives adaptation without burning members out.

The goal is to hit 10 calories as fast as possible each round, pushing past the sustainable effort threshold. The 1:00 recovery resets members enough to maintain that intensity across every hard interval.

days.cardio_note: Each round builds to a challenging Hard effort before coming back down — teaching the body to flush lactate and recover while still moving.

This ascending ladder repeats three times, training the body to approach and recover from its lactate threshold each round. That repeated stress and recovery is what drives aerobic adaptation and improves endurance over time.

Pairing fixed rest with a distance target encourages honest, consistent effort rather than pacing to a clock. Repeatedly hitting .2 miles at hard effort taxes the cardiovascular system in a way that makes sustained intensity more manageable with time/repetition.

days.cardio_note: Hard efforts sandwiched between moderate segments keep the body working aerobically even at rest, building toward a Max effort at the end. Remind members to protect the Moderate — it's what fuels the Max.

Three rounds of Moderate-to-Hard intervals raise the metabolic baseline before a Max effort finish. This forces the cardiovascular system to recruit efficiently under stress — the adaptation that makes hard efforts feel more manageable.

A calorie target trains members to find their most efficient output — push too little and the interval drags, push too hard and recovery feels short. That pacing awareness is a core driver of cardiovascular adaptation.

Four rounds of incomplete recovery – Moderate rest isn't full recovery by design.  Sustained aerobic stress forces the heart and muscles to become more efficient at clearing fatigure, which is where endurance gains are made.

The descending then re-ascending structure means the body never fully recovers, arriving at Max effort already taxed. That accumulated fatigue is the stimulus that builds real aerobic capacity and improves performance under stress.

A distance target makes output measurable and repeatable — coaches should encourage members to hit consistent splits each round rather than going all out early. Fading splits are a sign of poor pacing, steady splits are a sign of improving aerobic efficiency.

days.cardio_note: The moderate 2:00 is active work, not rest. The 1:00 hard effort pushes past where the body can sustain balance between effort and recovery, raising that ceiling over time. Consistent splits across all three rounds are the goal.

Each round steps up intentionally — easy, moderate, then hard. The first two intervals set up the 1:30, not slow it down. Consistent hard efforts across all three rounds are the measure of good pacing.
The 15-cal target gives members something to chase each round. Coaches should cue them to note their time and aim to repeat it. The 2:00 moderate is what fuels the next effort.

The short :45 easy intervals allow partial recovery without fully clearing the metabolic demand of the hard effort. This sustained accumulation is what drives cardiovascular adaptation. Coaches should cue members to commit fully to each Hard effort.

At 2:00, the hard effort is long enough that pacing matters — going out too hard compounds fatigue quickly. The 2:00 moderate maintains aerobic engagement without full recovery. Consistent hard splits across both rounds are the goal.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.1
days.cardio_note: The .3 mile cap gives everyone a fixed target to push through at their own pace, rather than a set time to fill. The full 2:00 recovery lets heart rate fully drop before the next repeat.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.2
days.cardio_note: Recovery here is Moderate, not Easy, so lactate never fully clears before the next Hard push. That's what builds tolerance for working while already fatigued.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.3
days.cardio_note: The 1-minute easy segment is only a partial reset, so the second Moderate/Hard wave starts already tired. That's the point — building the ability to push hard on legs that aren't fresh.

exercises.name: DB 1arm Lunge to Knee Drive Curl

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.4
days.cardio_note: Recovery is shorter than the work today, so members can't fully reset before the next push. It trains keeping intensity up without a full recovery.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.5
days.cardio_note: A calorie target instead of a time means the hard push is set by effort, not a fixed duration — it takes as long as it takes to hit 20 calories at real intensity.

exercises.name: Res. Band Diagonal Pull Apart Alt.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.6
days.cardio_note: Distance-based work ties intensity to individual capability instead of a fixed pace. The Moderate/Hard alternation trains the body to recover while moving — a different adaptation than steady-state cardio.

exercises.name: DB Chest Fly to Chest Press

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.7
days.cardio_note: Moderate should feel steady and breathable — short phrases still come easy. Hard should feel like a controlled push right at the edge, where talking is challenging.  That repeated exposure trains the body to buffer fatigue faster and hold that edge longer over time.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.8
days.cardio_note: Easy is a quick reset. Hard should feel like a controlled push right at the edge, sustainable for the full 2:00 but not comfortable. Repeating this 3x trains the body to recover fast and hit that edge repeatedly.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.9
days.cardio_note: 2:30 is long enough that hard has to be paced, not sprinted — members learn to hold an edge rather than spike and fade. Finishing on moderate instead of easy keeps the legs working through the comedown, so recovery becomes active instead of a full stop.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.10
days.cardio_note: Three quick shifts back to back force the body to switch fuel sources fast — aerobic for the steady stretches, anaerobic for the hard push — instead of settling into one system. That switching ability is what builds durable, well-rounded endurance over time.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.11
days.cardio_note: Calorie-based hard efforts are self-paced — the harder someone pushes, the faster they hit 25 and the sooner the interval ends. This rewards real intensity instead of just holding on for a fixed time, and keeps effort honest since easing off only makes the work last longer.

exercises.name: BW Reverse Lunge w/ Reach Alt.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.12
days.floor_note: Benchmark Day · 3 rounds. Round 1 is a lighter warm-up; round 2 sets your working weight; round 3 is the round that counts — log reps for each main lift.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.13
days.cardio_note: Equal work-to-work timing (no easy segment) means members shift straight from moderate into hard with no buffer, testing the ability to raise output on demand rather than ease into it.

exercises.name: DB Forward to Reverse Lunge Alt.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.14
days.cardio_note: The :30 max should feel truly all-out — unsustainable past 30 seconds, which is what recruits maximum fuel and muscle fiber. That ceiling is what separates max from hard, and why it can only last a short burst.

exercises.name: BW Reverse Lunge w/ Reach Alt.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.15
days.floor_note: Benchmark Day · 3 rounds. Round 1 is a lighter warm-up; round 2 sets your working weight; round 3 is the round that counts — log reps for each main lift.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.16
days.cardio_note: Short, repeated moderate-hard shifts train members to raise and lower output quickly without a real reset, building a different kind of fitness than steady-state cardio — quick, responsive shifts in effort rather than one sustained pace.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.17
days.cardio_note: A short calorie target at max effort means the push ends fast the harder someone works — rewarding true intensity over pacing it out. This trains the ability to spike output hard and briefly, then recover, rather than sustain a steady grind.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.18
days.cardio_note: Equal distance at two intensities means the hard segment always demands more from the body in less time than the moderate one — training members to raise power output while covering the same ground. Since it's distance-based, effort scales to each person's own fitness rather than a fixed pace.

exercises.name: DB Step Up to Reverse Lunge

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.19
days.cardio_note: After the hard push, effort drops to moderate instead of easy, so members recover while still working rather than getting a full reset. This trains the ability to hold quality effort even when tired, instead of needing a complete break to bounce back.

exercises.name: Slam Ball Roll Over Push Up
Ball Split Squat to Single Leg Deadlift

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.20
days.cardio_note: The longer moderate stretch builds aerobic capacity just below the limit, before the :40 hard push taps into anaerobic power for a real spike. The full easy reset lets the body recover completely, training a clean build-spike-recover cycle instead of stacking fatigue.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.21
days.cardio_note: Dropping to easy before the hard push means members hit that push from a recovered state rather than carrying fatigue into it, so the hard segment reflects true top-end output. This trains the ability to go from calm to a strong push quickly — a different demand than ramping up gradually.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.22
days.cardio_note: The long moderate stretch keeps members just below their limit, building aerobic capacity before the :45 hard push spikes into anaerobic effort. This 2:1 ratio is repeatable enough to hold quality across multiple rounds without breaking down.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.23
days.cardio_note: A short calorie target at hard effort is self-paced — the harder someone pushes, the faster they hit 10 and the sooner the push ends. This rewards true intensity over pacing it out, while the full 1:30 easy lets the body recover completely before the next round.

exercises.name: DB 1arm Snatch w/ Foot on Bench

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.24
days.cardio_note: The pre-fatigue from the moderate stretch teaches members that "tired" isn't "empty" — there's still a reserve available even when legs feel worn down. Cue members to trust that reserve and push through instead of easing off when pushing through Max.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.25
days.cardio_note: The gradual build primes the neuromuscular system in stages, so by the time members hit :30 max, the body is already firing efficiently and can recruit peak output faster. The 1:00 easy after clears fatigue fully before the next build, keeping quality consistent across all 4 rounds.

exercises.name: DB Chest Press and Fly Alt.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.26
days.cardio_note: Repeating the same short pattern builds pacing accuracy — members learn exactly what each intensity should feel like and can replicate it round after round instead of guessing. That consistency makes it easy to spot true fatigue setting in, since the pattern stays the same even as it gets harder to hit.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.27
days.cardio_note: With no easy segment between them, the jump from moderate to hard has to happen on command, not eased into — that is the test. Since hard lasts a full 1:30, members have to pace it rather than spike and fade, building control at sustained high effort.

exercises.name: DB 1  arm Clean with Step Up

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.28
days.cardio_note: Three rounds of moderate-hard-easy build pacing control before the closing :45 max, which tests what's still available after all that work. Cue members to give each hard effort everything it deserves, then trust that the body can still find more for that final max push.

exercises.name: DB Chest Press and Fly alt.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.29
days.cardio_note: Because the target stays the same each round but fatigue builds, hitting 10 cals takes longer as the set goes on — a visible sign of accumulating fatigue rather than a fixed pace. This trains members to keep pushing for the same output even as it gets harder to produce.

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.30
days.cardio_note: Repeating 1:30 hard efforts trains the body to buffer and clear lactate faster each round, raising the effort members can sustain before fatigue catches up. The closing moderate-to-easy taper eases heart rate down gradually instead of stopping cold, which helps the body recover more efficiently.

exercises.name: DB Step Up to Rev. Lunge

days.source_file: STUDIO RED HIIT Programming August 2026.pdf p.31
days.cardio_note: The moderate segment builds aerobic base before the hard push spikes into anaerobic effort, and the easy segment after lets the body clear lactate and heart rate drop before the pattern repeats. This full cycle trains build, spike, and recover as one complete unit
